messages:
tara: Quick sanity check — ran a weight-only INT8 run with bitsandbytes on replica-A and llm.int8 on replica-B for nova-13b. Observing a larger-than-expected quality delta on longform summarization slices. Anyone seen this pattern?
vikram: Can you paste the eval slice + full config?
tara: Pasted quick numbers below, will upload full run artifacts to the bucket in a bit.
```
Model: nova-13b
Backend A (bitsandbytes 8-bit weight-only):
 - avg_ppl: 12.4
 - rougeL_f1: 0.46
 - latency p95: 210ms
 - mem GPU: 7.8GB
Backend B (llm.int8 weight-only):
 - avg_ppl: 11.9
 - rougeL_f1: 0.50
 - latency p95: 260ms
 - mem GPU: 9.6GB
Eval slice: longform instructions (>=512 tokens), N=1k
Config notes: both runs used same tokenizer v2.1, no prompt templating differences, batching sim, kv-cache enabled.
```
jen: Interesting — bnb is faster + cheaper but seems to lose some F1 on longform. Did you enable per-channel quantization + the default 8bit-cookbook options?
tara: Yes per-channel true, used upstream bnb default for weight-only. No manual layer exclusion.
michael: Could be numerical drift in attention accumulation for long sequences. Try forcing fp16 for attention layers or do hybrid 16/8 for last N layers.
leo: Also check kv-cache dtype path — some backends keep cache in fp16, others in float32, that affects accumulation on long runs.
tara: Good call. I reran a tiny A/B with 1k tokens forcing kv-cache fp16 on both sides. New quick numbers: bnb rougeL_f1 0.48 (was 0.46), llm.int8 0.50. Latency gap held (~200ms vs 255ms). Memory: bnb up slightly.
vikram: Progress. If hybrid 16/8 recovers most of delta we may do a per-profile rollout: route short form -> bnb, longform -> llm.int8.
jen: Agreed, keep bnb as default for latency-sensitive routes but mark longform route as prefer-llmint8 until we validate hybrid quant schedule. Also add an eval regression alert on that longform slice.
devops-bot: Reminder: canary deploy started for nova-13b hybrid-quant profile @here
tara: Next steps: (1) run a larger sweep with hybrid last-4-layers fp16, (2) try freezing embeddings + output layer in bnb, (3) collect token-level divergence traces for failing examples. I'll open a GH issue with artifacts.
jen: Add cost delta numbers too — product wants to see latency vs $/req tradeoff.
michael: Hypothesis: bitsandbytes aggressive quant math optimizations enable a faster path but amplify rounding on long accumulation chains. If hybrid fixes it, we can publish a guidance doc: "bnb for short; hybrid for longform workloads." :thinking:
tara: Filed GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-evals/issues/412 (includes logs + eval csv). I'll schedule canary traffic split changes after the sweep.
leo: Also flag to Runtime: kernel fallback for attention math; might be worth instrumenting per-token error magnitude in dev console.
tara: Will follow up with a quick PR to console to show per-slice rouge deltas. Thanks all :thumbsup:
jen: Great thread. If sweep looks good we can add a default quant profile in Optimize to surface this recommendation. :shipit:
